pl-l2d42c1-d1e108.summary: Asks whether evil will and evil act in the same person concerning the same thing are one sin or different sins, as when one steals willingly: will and act differ, but are they different sins?

pl-l2d42c1-d1e111.summary: Reports some saying one sin, others different sins, since two different things are either two sins or two things that are not sins.

pl-l2d42c1-d1e114.summary: Reports the reply: they are two things, not two sins, but one sin, since one transgression or disobedience is committed in willing and acting, one contempt, lesser when in will alone, greater when the act is added; so the sin becomes greater, not plural.
claims: Will and act make one sin, increased by the act.

pl-l2d42c1-d1e118.summary: Objects: if they are one sin, the one who acts after willing is guilty of nothing beyond what he was guilty of in will alone, since one is guilty of eternal death only for sin, and no other sin is committed by the act.

pl-l2d42c1-d1e121.summary: Reports the answer: he is guilty only for sin, and though will and act are one sin, by acting he becomes guilty for something else than before, namely the act, which differs from the will though not another sin.
claims: Guilt extends to the act without a second sin.

pl-l2d42c1-d1e124.summary: Objects further: they are different sins as transgressions of different commands, 'do not steal' forbidding the act and 'do not covet your neighbor's goods' the will.

pl-l2d42c1-d1e127.summary: Reports the answer: the commands are different and forbid the two distinctly, as Augustine on Exodus teaches, yet one transgression and one sin is incurred in breaking them, as conversely the two commands of charity command two to be loved, yet one charity is commended.
claims: One transgression can break two commands.

pl-l2d42c1.summary: Asks whether evil will and evil act concerning the same thing are one sin or two. Some say two, since will and act differ; others say one sin, one transgression and contempt, lesser in will alone and greater when the act is added. Objection: then the thief who acts after willing is guilty of nothing new; answer: he becomes guilty for the act, which differs from the will, though it is not another sin. Objection: will and act violate different commands ('do not steal,' 'do not covet'); answer: two commands forbid them distinctly, yet one transgression is incurred, as the two commands of charity commend one charity.
claims: Will and act are different, but some hold they form one sin.
On that view, adding the act enlarges the sin without multiplying it.
The doer becomes guilty for the act, though it is not another sin.
Two commands can forbid will and act while one transgression is incurred.
The two commands of charity commend one charity.
